header.what: One run of Klaxon's diagnosis agent on the case poison-message: claude-opus-5-5 through Claude Code on Aravind's seat (live). Its tools read incident data captured from Klaxon's live stack.

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer is stuck on one poison message, provider-events/0@229 (evt_000681, pay_000619), whose amount is invalid ('amount must be positive integer cents'). ledger-consumer was recreated at 07:56:08Z with BAD_EVENTS=retry, 5 s before the event arrived. It retries that message forever (attempt 13, every 15 s) and never commits past offset 229. Events behind it pile up, so ledger lag grows (176 at the alert, 222 at c1) and the money check cannot settle: BooksBehindProvider. payment-confirmer uses BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, so it dead-lettered the same message and stayed at lag 0. Still open: what exactly is wrong with evt_000681's amount and why the provider sent a second event for an already-succeeded payment, what BAD_EVENTS was before 07:56, and who changed it.

evidence.shows: The money check could not run: after 60 s the ledger still had 222 messages not handled, against 176 at the alert. payment-confirmer had 0, so only the ledger is stuck.

ledger-consumer logs the same error over and over: 'could not book; will retry the same message' for provider-events/0@229, error 'amount must be positive integer cents', attempt 13, retrying every 15 s.
ledger-consumer was recreated at 07:56:08Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=retry. payment-confirmer uses BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter. All other services were last deployed at 07:52:06Z.
The first failure on 0@229 was at 07:56:13Z, just after the redeploy. payment-confirmer dead-lettered the same message for the same invalid-amount reason and moved on.
webhook-receiver queued the message at offset 229 as event evt_000681, key pay_000619, and returned 200.

pay_000619 already had a valid event, evt_000680 (payment.succeeded, 1260 cents), at offset 228. Both consumers handled it. payments-api created pmt_000619 with a correct amount in cents, so evt_000681 is an extra event with a bad amount.

proposed_fix.summary: Set BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter on ledger-consumer, the same as payment-confirmer, and recreate the container, or roll back to its previous settings. It will then dead-letter 0@229 and work through the backlog. Watch the ledger lag fall to 0 and rerun the money check. After that, review evt_000681 in the dead-letter queue by hand: ask the provider what it is, and book it only if it turns out to be a real event. Also find out who changed BAD_EVENTS to retry at 07:56 and why.

diagnosis.blast_radius: This affects only ledger-consumer. Dead-lettering means any event the ledger cannot book is set aside instead of blocking, so the ledger may stay short by that event until someone handles it. The money check would flag that gap. Restarting the consumer reprocesses messages after its last committed offset. LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent should keep those from being booked twice.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Set BAD_EVENTS back to retry and recreate ledger-consumer. Dead-lettered messages stay in the dead-letter topic and can be replayed into the ledger once the cause is understood.
